partners.mechanism_chain: CYB5R3 variant (HGNC:2593) —DISRUPTS→ Methemoglobin reductase (HGNC:2593); Methemoglobin reductase (HGNC:2593) —LEADS_TO→ Methemoglobin reduction (GO:0006076); Methemoglobin reduction (GO:0006076) —DECREASES→ Methemoglobin (CHEBI:27772); Methemoglobin (CHEBI:27772) —LEADS_TO→ Methemoglobinemia (HP:0001764); SLC2A1 variant (HGNC:10564) —DISRUPTS→ Glucose transporter 1 (HGNC:10564); Glucose transporter 1 (HGNC:10564) —LEADS_TO→ Glucose transport in red blood cell (GO:0015894); Glucose transport in red blood cell (GO:0015894) —DECREASES→ Glucose in red blood cell (CHEBI:17234); Glucose in red blood cell (CHEBI:17234) —DECREASES→ Pentose phosphate pathway (KEGG:hsa00010); Pentose phosphate pathway (KEGG:hsa00010) —DECREASES→ NADPH (CHEBI:15361); NADPH (CHEBI:15361) —DECREASES→ Methemoglobin reduction (GO:0006076); Glucose transporter 1 (HGNC:10564) —LEADS_TO→ Glucose transport in brain (GO:0006079); Glucose transport in brain (GO:0006079) —DECREASES→ Glucose in brain (CHEBI:17234); Glucose in brain (CHEBI:17234) —DECREASES→ Neuronal energy metabolism (GO:0045747); Neuronal energy metabolism (GO:0045747) —LEADS_TO→ Encephalopathy (HP:0001295). Loss-of-function variants in CYB5R3 lead to impaired methemoglobin reduction, causing methemoglobinemia. Concurrently, loss-of-function variants in SLC2A1 impair glucose transport into red blood cells and neurons. Reduced glucose in red blood cells leads to decreased flux through the pentose phosphate pathway, diminishing NADPH production, which is essential for CYB5R3 activity in methemoglobin reduction. Impaired glucose transport into neurons compromises neuronal energy metabolism, resulting in encephalopathy. Thus, both diseases converge on compromised cellular energy and redox homeostasis, with NADPH being a key shared metabolite linking the two pathways.

Thus, both diseases converge on compromised cellular energy and redox homeostasis, with NADPH being a key shared metabolite linking the two pathways.

**How to falsify it:** The presence of common, highly penetrant variants in CYB5R3 and SLC2A1, respectively, in the general population (e.g., gnomAD allele frequency > 0.1%) would challenge the proposed causal link if these variants do not segregate with the respective disease phenotypes. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap highlights the critical role of glucose metabolism and NADPH homeostasis in both red blood cell function and neuronal health. Therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring NADPH levels or improving glucose utilization could potentially benefit patients with either condition, suggesting a potential for repurposing treatments or developing novel therapeutic approaches targeting these shared metabolic pathways.
